summary: Phased mini-flood surge causing reserved-pool attach lag and KV-prefetch amplification
description: AtlasAI reported recurrent midday throughput hill on their dedicated reserved pool. Symptoms include increased p99 latency for batched routes, frequent GPU attach latency spikes (~200-800ms), and transient autoscaler shrink/failover cycles. Customer traffic pattern: large number of very short inference requests from a background ingestion worker that phases in waves every 3-7 minutes. We suspect a phased "mini-flood" of tiny short-lived streams interacting with KV-prefetch growth and the allocator's heartbeat smoothing logic.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs ~3000 short requests/min across 20 clients in waves (15s on / 165s idle) to dedicated pool
2) Requests are short (avg tokens 15) and open streaming connections briefly; many retry on 429s
3) Observe allocator attach latency and autoscaler decisions in prod/us-east during the wave window
4) Correlate with kv-cache metrics and prefetch lease counts (see metrics_references).
observed_behavior: During wave start: rapid growth in open short streams -> KV-prefetch lease count jumps 2-3x, allocator reports attach latency up to 800ms, autoscaler triggers temporary shrink then rapid grow leading to oscillation. Customer sees p50 stable but p95/p99 spike and occasional 5xx throttles for a small percentage of requests.
expected_behavior: Stable attach latency <= 100ms for reserved pool routes, autoscaler should not oscillate on short-lived microbursts, KV-prefetch should not amplify lease churn for low-context short requests.
investigation_notes: Checked allocator logs (allocator-us-east-2) during window: several attach reattempts and 'prefetch lease limit' warnings around 11:22-11:38 UTC
Grafana trace linked shows backlog on nvme_io_wait correlated with KV write amplification (dashboard: ReservedPool->I/O->nvme_io_wait)
Autoscaler metrics show shrink events following attach latency crossing 400ms threshold; cooldown timers were insufficient for this microburst pattern
Customer SDK uses aggressive connection pooling with short-lived connections; increases ephemeral client processes during waves (reported by AtlasAI support engineer)
Hypothesis: many short streams cause repeated KV-prefetch entries and lease churn which increases IO, slowing attach path and triggering autoscaler reflexive behavior
resolution_notes: Workaround provided: asked AtlasAI to enable connection reuse and increase client-side batching for background workers; recommended smoothing their wave schedule to reduce simultaneous short streams. Engineering mitigation: disabled autoscaler shrink-on-attach-latency for reserved pools for a temporary cooldown window and applied a quick fix to decrement KV-prefetch aggressive prewarm for short-stream routes. Change deployed to staging and then rolled to us-east canary.
root_cause: Interaction between phased microburst short-stream pattern from customer clients and conservative autoscaler shrink policy combined with KV-prefetch lease amplification leading to NVMe IO backlog; allocator attach path delayed, prompting autoscaler oscillation and transient throughput degradation.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-allocator: implement smoothing window for attach-latency-based autoscaler decisions (https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/issues/512)
ENG-kv: add adaptive prefetch throttle for low-context short streams
DX: publish best-practice guide for customers on background worker connection reuse and wave-smoothing
SRE: monitor reserved-pool attach latency with new alert threshold for recurring patterns
